extracted.intended_audience: in-house counsel, compliance officers, investor relations teams, and corporate communications professionals at public companies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and best practices for public companies to comply with Regulation FD when disclosing material nonpublic information, with a focus on website and social media use and preventing/selectively disclosing information. Includes factors for establishing recognized channels of distribution and recommended corporate controls and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation FD prohibition on selective disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation FD prohibits public companies, or persons acting on their behalf, from selectively disclosing material nonpublic information to certain securities professionals or to shareholders who might trade on the basis of the information before such information has been disseminated to the general public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to prevent selective disclosure to a 'privileged few' and provide equal access to company information. A company that inadvertently discloses material nonpublic information may cure the violation by making prompt public disclosure of the information (typically within 24 hours).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public dissemination standard — recognized channel of distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Information is considered public for Regulation FD purposes if it has been disseminated through a recognized channel of distribution that results in broad, non-exclusionary distribution to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadly disseminated press releases and Form 8-K filings are the accepted default channels for distributing material information to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2008 Guidance factor — whether and how company has informed investors it will post important information
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and how a company has informed investors and the markets that it will post important information on its website (or other digital channel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making clear, advance notice to the market that a particular website or channel will be used to post material information supports finding the channel is a recognized distribution method.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2008 Guidance factor — pattern or practice of posting important information
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the company has a pattern or practice of posting important information on its website (or designated channel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent historical use to post material information makes it more likely the channel will be treated as recognized for Regulation FD.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2008 Guidance factor — site/channel navigation and prominence of disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the website or channel efficiently leads investors and the markets to information about the company, including investor-specific information, and whether the information is prominently disclosed in a consistent location and in a format that is readily accessible to the general public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information should be easy to find, in a consistent location and format, to support broad public accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2008 Guidance factor — whether posted information is picked up and reported by media/market
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which information posted on the website (or channel) is routinely picked up by the market and readily available to, and reported by, the media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the market and media routinely report material posted on the channel, that supports its being a recognized distribution channel.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2008 Guidance factor — steps taken to make information accessible or to alert the market
rubrics_metrics.description: Steps the company has taken to make information posted on its website (or channel) accessible or to alert the market of its availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active steps (e.g., notices, cross-posts, alerts) help demonstrate the company is using the channel to broadly disseminate information.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2008 Guidance factor — whether the website/channel is kept current and accurate
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the website or channel is kept current and accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining up-to-date content and accuracy supports reliance on the channel as a recognized means of distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2008 Guidance factor — use of other distribution methods and predominance
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the company uses other methods to distribute important information and the extent to which those other methods are the predominant method used by the company to disseminate information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If traditional channels (press releases, filings) remain predominant, an alternate channel is less likely to be treated as recognized absent other supporting factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2008 Guidance factor — the nature of the information
rubrics_metrics.description: The nature of the information being disclosed (i.e., whether it is material and what type of information it is).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain types of information may be more or less likely to be considered appropriate for dissemination via a given channel depending on sensitivity/market impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media channels — steps required to establish them as recognized distribution channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies that want to use social media and avoid Regulation FD challenges need to take appropriate steps to establish the social media channel as a recognized channel of distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to the 2008 Guidance factors, companies should alert the market about (1) the forms of social media or other communication channels the company will use to disclose material nonpublic information and (2) the type of information the company intends to disclose through these identified communication channels (per the 2013 Report/Netflix guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly identify and communicate recognized channels of distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should clearly identify their recognized channels of distribution for disclosure of material nonpublic information and communicate these channels to any third-party service providers engaged to produce website and social media content on their behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly naming channels and ensuring vendors/PR firms know which accounts are Regulation FD–compliant prevents inadvertent selective disclosures (DraftKings failed to identify CEO personal accounts as FD-compliant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Designate authorized spokespersons and control third-party/posting access
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should limit disclosures of material nonpublic information on social media to authorized spokespersons and control access by third-party service providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approaches vary from prohibiting social-media disclosure of material nonpublic information to requiring advance approval and allowing only authorized persons to post. Policies should cover third-party PR firms and personal accounts used on the company's behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quiet period policies — scope and relationship to Regulation FD
rubrics_metrics.description: Quiet period policies (often included in a company's Regulation FD policy) apply to all forms of communication during the sensitive period before quarterly financial results are publicly released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quiet period policies are designed to prevent Regulation FD violations but do not prohibit the public release of material information if done in a Regulation FD–compliant manner (i.e., via recognized channels).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadvertent disclosure cure requirement — public dissemination required
rubrics_metrics.description: An inadvertent disclosure of material nonpublic information may only be cured through public dissemination of the inadvertently disclosed information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simply taking down or removing the selectively disclosed content is insufficient to cure a Regulation FD violation. An inadvertent selective disclosure can constitute a violation even if it was available only briefly (in this case 30 minutes). Prompt public disclosure (typically within 24 hours) is necessary to cure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular review of channels to ensure ongoing Regulation FD compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should regularly review their ongoing practices with respect to website and social media channels to ensure that any previously identified channels of distribution remain Regulation FD–compliant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodic reassessment ensures that changes in media use, platform behavior, or company practices do not unintentionally undermine a channel's recognized status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing training and reminders for officers, employees, and third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should periodically remind senior officers, employees, and relevant third-party service providers about the requirements of Regulation FD policies and related disclosure restrictions imposed by the federal securities laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training reduces the risk of inadvertent selective disclosures; include PR firms and other vendors in training and communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand enforcement risk and potential penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation FD violations can result in enforcement actions and civil penalties (e.g., DraftKings agreed to pay a US$200,000 civil penalty to settle the charges).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that even brief or inadvertent selective disclosures can lead to enforcement and penalties; include enforcement risk in compliance risk assessments.
